newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: BolsWessanen warns of more charges.
newsitem.headline: BolsWessanen warns of more charges.

text.p: Dutch food and drinks group BolsWessanen NV said on Wednesday it maintained its earlier announced expectation that net income from ordinary activities over full 1996 would fall by about 10 percent.
It added that restructuring currently underway or being prepared would result in additional extraordinary charges of 10 to 15 million guilders in the second 1996 half.
The company's 1996 first-half net from ordinary operations fell by 21.6 percent to 68.9 million guilders from 87.9 million in the year-ago period.
This year's result was further dampened by a 5.4 million guilder extraordinary charge, which depressed the total net profit figure to 63.5 million.
The one-off charge included a loss on the sale of BolsWessanen's German drinks maker Strothmann earlier this year. In May BolsWessanen said this transaction would result in a small book loss.
First-half turnover fell by 2.2 percent to 2.30 billion guilders which was caused by selling non-core activities.
Operating profit fell by 21.2 percent to 96.4 million guilders from 122.4 million in the first six months of 1995.
The company said this decrease was caused by deteriorating results of its cereals business, lower exports of spirits and falling margins on its U.S. dairy activities.

In 1995, BolsWessanen posted a full-year net profit from ordinary operations of 202.9 million guilders, down from 254.1 million in the previous year. The total 1995 net after one-off items was 205.8 million compared with 254.1 million in 1994.
